head: 07bc014beea58bb6c96cc6461aaa1256ef6fa41b
summary:
Four of the five defects from the first review are fixed, and the fifth (a fail/block review leaving earlier approval active) is fixed when the wake runs:
- Every outcome wake now withdraws earlier authorization (pending status, then disabling auto-merge) before fresh checks.
- A fail/block review returns the issue to bare `doing`, preserving unrelated labels.
- Per-PR index errors no longer abort the queue.
- Extra closing keywords and references are refused, and the squash commit text is fixed to `Closes #N`.
- The findings publisher authenticates negative receipts from failed jobs but still rejects a pass receipt from a failed job.
- The hosted control workflow now includes the security tests and refuses skipped tests.

Two correctness defects remain in the wake and retry paths, so the PR fails.

1. Sharing the repository-wide `issue-ci-handoff` concurrency group across two different workflows lets each workflow's queued run cancel the other's pending run. This loses CI failure handoffs and also outcome wakes, including withdrawal and the return to doing.
2. The outcome writer checks its own run with `producer_identity`, which requires a default-branch head branch and a same-repository head. `pull_request_target` runs very likely report the PR head branch and head repository, so PR metadata and head-change wakes would be refused before any withdrawal or reconciliation. This path is untested because the test mocks the check.

requirement_results.evidence: The claude-review action is pinned through AW_ACTION_REF. collect() and gate_evidence() require every configured gate to succeed at the exact head and base, with trusted workflow IDs and blobs. Policy comes from action.trusted_policy on the default branch. invoke_json passes --tools '' and an empty strict MCP configuration, and supplies only data fetched through the API.

native_merge.enqueue runs: pending status, then QUEUE with expectedHeadOid and SQUASH, then re-verification, then success. base_rules requires an active strict ruleset with the integration-bound status and no bypass actors. linked_issue allows one canonical 'Closes #N' line and rejects other closing keywords in the title or body. commitHeadline/commitBody are fixed to 'Merge PR #N'/'Closes #N'. policy() enforces the qualification hold (lifecycle_mode full and empty blockers).

return_doing adds bare 'doing' before removing todo/done. Each step re-verifies the receipt, head, issue contract hash, open state and both blocked spellings. Unrelated labels are preserved and interrupted updates recover (test_review_lifecycle.py). The template and writer_contract bind the issue-ci-handoff group; see the finding about cross-workflow pending replacement.

claude_review.main returns 1 for non-pass decisions after printing the receipt. verify_result_receipt(allow_rejected=True) accepts a failed job only for fail/block decisions. claude_findings.main now accepts failure wakes. Tests cover a negative receipt from a failed job and refusal of a pass receipt from a failed job.

reconcile withdraws approval for every open PR before indexing and isolates per-PR errors, and the index no longer raises on untitled or unknown runs. However, sharing the cross-workflow concurrency group can cancel pending outcome wakes (template line 18). pull_request_target wakes are likely refused in main() by producer_identity's default-branch check (native_merge.py ~381). Either way, withdrawal and reconciliation can be skipped for real metadata, head or issue changes.

native-auto-merge-controls.yml discovers both plugins/faberline/skills/issue-ci/tests and scripts/security/tests and fails on skipped tests or zero tests. Hosted runs 40743480102 and 40743487860 succeeded at this head. Templates and docs keep placeholder IDs for the later rollout step.
No thresholds or blockers change. test_a_green_review_with_a_coverage_hold_cannot_queue_merge shows the coverage hold is honoured.

The provenance packet shows the final-review source descends from c9ec41e, and scripts/security/* and other inherited files are unchanged from it. guarded_merge and the 'merge' operation stay hard-disabled, and the guarded-merge template is unchanged.

findings.title: Sharing issue-ci-handoff across two workflows lets pending replacement drop CI handoff and outcome wakes
findings.detail: GitHub concurrency groups are repository-wide across workflows. With cancel-in-progress false, a newly queued run cancels any previously pending run in the same group. The existing handoff template justifies pending replacement only because every handoff wake reconciles all managed PRs. Now an outcome-writer run can replace a pending CI handoff run, losing a CI failure→todo handoff until the next test completion; this changes existing CI behaviour. Conversely, a handoff run can replace a pending outcome run (an issue contract edit, review start or new head). That outcome's withdrawal or return to doing then never runs until some later outcome wake, so an earlier success status or native request can remain active and a rejection is not reflected in the lifecycle.
findings.required_fix: Keep serialization but make it lossless across both writers. For example, have each workflow also run the other's full reconciliation on every wake, or merge both into one writer workflow. Add tests where a pending wake of each workflow is replaced by the other.

findings.title: Outcome writer self-identity check likely refuses all pull_request_target wakes
findings.detail: main() calls review.producer_identity for the current run with EVENTS. producer_identity requires run.head_branch == default_branch and head_repository == repo. For pull_request_target runs, GitHub reports the PR's head branch, head SHA and head repository, which may be a fork. Every PR opened/synchronize/edited/ready_for_review/converted_to_draft wake would therefore exit with an error before withdrawing approval or reconciling the queue, contrary to the documented PR-metadata wake behaviour. test_entrypoint_checks_merge_producer_and_surfaces_unknown_writes mocks producer_identity, so this path is untested.
findings.required_fix: Authenticate the writer run per event type. For pull_request_target, verify the workflow definition blob at the base/default-branch commit rather than the PR head branch or repository. Add an entrypoint test that runs the real identity check for each trigger event.

uncertainties: The pull_request_target finding assumes GitHub's run metadata reports the PR head branch and head repository for those runs; this was not verified live.

The findings publisher still uses the default latest-run-across-all-PRs selector. A negative receipt may be unreadable to it whenever another PR's review run starts first. This behaviour was already in c9ec41e.
